note: Bridger-Teton NF campground in a dense aspen grove on the peninsula at the narrows of New Fork Lake, on the edge of the Wind River Range 25 miles from Pinedale; the last 5 miles are on New Fork Lake Road, gravel and rough but passable in two-wheel drive. Turnarounds in the campground are narrow: the Forest Service does not recommend oversized vehicles and trailers. Campground host on site; no trash service. New Fork Trail into the Bridger Wilderness starts at the entrance; concrete boat ramp under a mile away. --Claude
summary: FS + rec.gov + catalog read: 19 sites (4 reservable: 7, 8, 15, 18), 25 ft (site 15 30 ft), no hookups, vault toilets, no water, $12 (all written manual). Lakeview holds (FS 'most sites afford scenic lake views'); site 18 a lakefront lead (~40 m over open sage). ACCESS-WORDING flag: 'oversized vehicles and trailers are not recommended'. Phone empty -> 307-367-4326. Pin fine. Season unstated (FS 'June 1st').
flags: ACCESS WORDING (reviewer's call; possible drop candidate under the 'trailers not recommended' rule): recreation.gov notice 'Turnarounds in the campground are narrow, oversized vehicles and trailers are not recommended'. Against it: the catalog permits RV/Trailer/Fifth Wheel on every site with Max Vehicle Length 25 ft (30 ft at site 15), and the access road is 'suitable for two wheel drive vehicles' though rough. A 23-ft motorhome is not oversized by the catalog's own lengths; the wording reads as aimed at big rigs and trailers.

WATERFRONT LEAD (not changed; stored lakeview holds - FS/rec.gov 'most sites afford scenic lake views'): site 18 (reservable, sold by the night) sits at the edge of an open sagebrush slope ~40 m from the top of the east arm's bare beach band (high-water edge), ~48 m to the imaged waterline; site 15 (reservable) ~50 m, partly through trees. One or two sites at the ~50 m bound - lakefront-with-caveat is the reviewer's call; catalog points only, not ground-truthed.
